paras: The attempted lynching of Bruce at Dardanelle took place on a Sunday night in December 1880, when a body of fifty men tried to take a prisoner named Bruce from his guards at the jail in Dardanelle, Arkansas, in order to lynch him. Prosecuting Attorney McKennon and the county officers intervened, and the attempt failed.

According to The Russellville Democrat, Bruce killed John White by cutting his throat on the preceding Thursday night at a place four miles from Dardanelle. The paper described the killing as "the result of a drunken brawl" and gave no race for either man. Bruce was arrested and lodged in the jail at Dardanelle.

On the following Sunday night, which by the paper's dating was December 12, a body of fifty men came to take the prisoner from the guards "for the purpose of lynching him." The Democrat wrote that the men would have succeeded but for "the prompt intervention in behalf of the prisoner" by Prosecuting Attorney McKennon and the officers of the county. Bruce stayed in custody, and no injuries or arrests of the would-be lynchers were reported.
The coverage does not show an indictment, trial or other outcome for Bruce in White's death, and it names none of the fifty men.

The episode survives in a single unheadlined paragraph in The Russellville Democrat of December 16, 1880, printed among Christmas advertisements and social notes. The item stated the killing as fact, gave no races, and credited the officials, not the mob, as the paper told it. No wire version or report from another paper was found, and the collection holds no Black-press coverage from this period.

accounts.label: Local newspaper report
accounts.gist: Bruce killed White in a drunken brawl, was jailed, and fifty men tried to take him from the guards to lynch him; the prosecuting attorney and county officers stopped them.

framing.detail: A short unheadlined local item that states the killing as fact, names no race, and credits the officials' 'prompt intervention in behalf of the prisoner'.

record_check.dossier: Dardanelle is in Yell County; A1 names no county, and other Russellville Democrat items on a separate 1881 Dardanelle case call the jailed men 'of Yell county'.
No race is given for Bruce or John White; nothing in the coverage shows this was anti-Black violence.
Supported: Bruce was held by guards in the Dardanelle jail.
